title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input Sanitization and Deterministic Verification
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate reuse, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest [14]).

sections.introduction: LLM-driven automation promises productivity gains for network operations (NetOps) by translating high-level operator intent into device CLI. However, deployment safety requires assurances beyond surface-text similarity: sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, and topology-dependent invariants must hold before pushing configurations. Deterministic validators that operate over explicit network models (reachability, precedence, required sequences) are a natural deployment gate, but the net benefit of coupling template-based input sanitization and bounded automated repair with verifier-gating has not been quantified under a preregistered estimand framework. We therefore ask a sharply scoped question amenable to preregistered confirmatory inference: under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one LLM draft per intent reused across conditions), does template-based sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating with at-most-one automated repair change the paired rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? To address this, we executed a preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-03), archived the end-to-end execution and analysis artifacts, and report artifact-grounded quantitative inference with explicit protocol disclosures.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) enable fast, semantics-focused checks of forwarding and policy invariants and are commonly proposed as deployment gates for configuration changes [5–7]. Prior NetOps evaluations of LLMs typically report string- or reference-match metrics that do not directly measure deployability or validator acceptance; such surface metrics can misrepresent operational risk because they ignore ordering and reachability constraints [3,8,9]. Work on generate–validate–repair architectures demonstrates that integrating external checks and constrained repair improves outcome metrics on narrow tasks, but effectiveness depends on precise verifier diagnostics and bounded repair policies [11,3]. Security literature documents prompt-injection and indirect attacks on LLM-integrated applications, motivating defenses such as input sanitization and deterministic gating [10, Not What You've Signed Up For]. Surveys of AIOps and LLM-for-telecommunications synthesize these trends and call for operationally grounded benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than token overlap [4, W4411735779]. Our study contributes a preregistered, artifact-backed measurement that uses deterministic-validator acceptance as the primary estimand and enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics so that downstream pipeline elements (sanitization, gating, permitted repair) are the causal factors under test.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The primary preregistered estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome is 1 if the deterministic validator accepts the final candidate produced by the pipeline variant and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (all analysis parameters were archived). Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents producing paired episodes (Baseline vs Guarded). The synthetic intent templates exercise safe sequencing patterns (shutdown–modify–restore), MTU/VLAN changes, protected-interface rules, and uplink switchover semantics. The adversary applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates; task manifests, generation seeds, and mutation taxonomy are archived. Model, validator, and orchestration. The declared generator is gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing the guarded pipeline. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); we disclose this as a protocol deviation because provider defaults can affect sampling determinism. Pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate. Generation semantics were preregistered as shared_initial_candidate. Per pair the pipeline timeline was: (1) task instantiation and adversarial mutation; (2) single shared initial LLM call producing the shared_initial_candidate; (3) Baseline scoring: validator applied to the shared_initial_candidate; (4) Guarded branch: template-based sanitizer applied and, if policy permitted, at-most-one automated repair LLM call allowed; (5) final validation and guarded decision. The design therefore isolates downstream sanitizer/gate/repair effects applied to the same initial draft rather than differences in initial generation. Missingness, exclusions, and analysis plan. The preregistered missingness rule excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; complete_pairs_included = 141. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar); bootstrap CI parameters are archived. Provider-call accounting and reconciliation. Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 156, completed_model_calls = 147, failed_model_calls = 9, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. These counts support the shared_initial_candidate semantics and track the at-most-one permitted repair events.
sections.results: Execution summary and primary counts. The run completed 282 of 300 planned episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons recorded under the preregistered missingness rules, yielding 141 complete pairs for primary analysis. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. Condition-level acceptance. Condition summaries: baseline_successes = 135/141 (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141/141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). Paired contingency and inference. The paired contingency table is n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Discordant-case diagnostics. All six discordant (n10) pairs are traceable in the archived per-episode validator traces; reconciliation links each discordant pair to a permitted repair-stage event (repair-stage count = 6). In each discordant case sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted repair converted a draft the baseline validator rejected into a final candidate the validator accepted. Sensitivity to missingness. As a conservative sensitivity (not the preregistered primary analysis), treating the nine both-missing pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400. This recalculation illustrates the effect of technical failures on marginal rates but does not change the paired-contingency inference on included pairs. All numeric results, the contingency table, and per-episode diagnostic traces are archived and reproducible from the execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the execution manifest [14].
sections.discussion: Estimand reconciliation and interpretation. The preregistration natural-language hypothesis suggested that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success; the registered formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct constructs: deterministic-validator acceptance is an operational, semantics-focused proxy for deployability but does not directly equal attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle. In our run the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by ≈4.255 percentage points because sanitizer plus bounded repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. That outcome is consistent with an operator-focused benefit (reduced rework for reparable drafts) but does not imply measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Repair–gate co-design implications. The six discordant pairs show repairs enabling acceptance; this is desirable when repairs preserve intended semantics but risky if repairs mask adversarial manipulations. Operational deployment therefore requires joint specification of: (1) the validator's semantic coverage (what invariants are enforced), (2) the sanitizer's allowed normalization rules, and (3) the repair policy and permitted edit class. Narrow, conservative repair scopes that only address syntactic or canonicalization errors are lower-risk than unconstrained semantic rewrites. Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and triggered the preregistered exclusion rule. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing, and protected-interface invariants but omits some dynamic protocol-level semantics; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: evaluation used a single generator (gpt-5-mini), a single validator, and synthetic intent templates, limiting generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the absolute numerical effect is small relative to a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical detectability (p = 0.03125) should not be conflated with broad operational impact without larger, multi-model, and attacker-centric follow-ups. Reproducibility guidance and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset). To produce deterministic reproduction runs we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 for both shared initial generation and any permitted repair calls; the execution manifest and analysis artifacts contain the complete run record necessary for re-execution. Recommendations. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or reachability tests; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects; (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction; (5) narrowly bound automated repair scopes and require conservative repair policies when validator coverage is partial.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics tie the six discordant pairs to permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to a measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions without an independent semantic-safety oracle. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims reported here are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts; the execution manifest is the primary machine-verifiable archive and is cited below as [14].

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
